Majority of Germans: We Don't Have a Real Democracy

...and yet I still wish we had the German political system in Canada. It definitely seems like a step up from what we have right now.

I kinda wish the article went into a little more detail. What are the problems of the German system, and what could perhaps be done differently? For now, having proportional representation seems like a good idea. No more "majority" governments for the Tories or Liberals, please.

What's wrong with the implementation of democracy in Germany is hard to answer in short, there are many factors that can be considered problematic or not depending on your position.

One obvious problem is that - as currently demonstrated by the ruling government - it is possible for the government to violate the Grundrecht (german constitution) and get away with it at least some of the time. But that's a problem in any democracy I am aware of and much more excessive in some prominent cases such as the USA.

Another problem is one that all democracies share: Engagement of the people in politics. It has become the default to consider voting as fulfilling your political duties. Once every few years putting a cross on a piece of paper is not going to be enough to ensure a healthy balance of power within a state. Sadly a large portion of the population seems to assume that by voting they have done all they can be expected to do. Another large portion doesn't even vote. In the meantime there are people within the government that work hard to acquire more power, using the apathy of the people as opportunity. It should be obvious that this can't work out well, but we are living in the century of the self and investing time into anything that is not immediately beneficial to your selfish needs it completely out of the question, right?
